'''Karl Brandan Mollweide''' (3 February 1774 &ndash; 10 March 1825) was a [[German people|German]] [[mathematician]]<ref name="Sullivan2006">{{cite book|last=Sullivan|first=Michael|title=Precalculus|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=FK7v2a-HSB4C|accessdate=27 September 2011|date=2006-01-01|publisher=Pearson Custom Publishing|isbn=978-0-536-91924-3|page=680}}</ref> and [[astronomer]] who taught in [[Halle (Saale)|Halle]] and [[Leipzig]]. In [[trigonometry]], he rediscovered the formula now known as [[Mollweide's formula]]. He invented a [[map projection]] called the [[Mollweide projection]].[[File:Karl_Mollweide.png|thumb|Karl Mollweide]]
